question.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=4x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-6y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/040ac76a28687db1c99d3379242b726a85aa4baf269a7c6d35d9662af1d3bd78.png)
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/0c10626785034f566b65778fad63032e3a9ad8cc2c884bc3da3e88fdff3db50b.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/18d25c282ee921144387d9c30e19a461746271a44cab929ab8075190b0f5c16e.svg)

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_1=4$ with the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/e99452a0ae70ad466de402da561590e4fc3b0de089fa0f74818a1986cadfbd42.svg)

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_2=-6$ with the corresponding eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/50b227b577144e091543a383e38d0d74a02193b8372fec1eddcfa75d06d3878b.svg)

The general solution of the system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/0ee79c93c2e488563f7515fb0ec6b30d5cb2b41795d23f0b9d4699338edcc92c.svg)

Now, notice that:

- The straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/f10a5247f1d1b5df56adab19d1dd64e9edbc04fb5615db365f62b1eebda40dc7.svg)
lie on the $x$-axis. Since $e^{4t} \to \infty$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t \to \infty.$

- The straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/517dcfcf2467960dd5d35d9676c86c4bf0f66e0c4f13ccd99e862816efed675e.svg)
lie on the $y$-axis. Since $e^{-6t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$

Among the given options, the only phase portrait satisfying these conditions is the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/91c074766b92790a0e78b768b0290d7723617d6ed30e51e842501cad63e58a44.png)
